evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: 10.21 mg/L at t=239.0 h, then 1.92 mg/L at t=240.0 h — abrupt collapse
Receiving online DO2 sensor, t=240–259 h: all 20 readings below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit; last value 1.46 mg/L at t=259 h; mean of last 10 = 1.61 mg/L; linear drift -0.022 mg/L/h
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 0.02 g/L @119 h, 0.95 g/L @179 h, 2.62 g/L @239 h — metabolically active batch, not product-limited
submission.rationale: Receiving DO collapsed from ~10.2 mg/L (t=239 h) to ~1.9 mg/L (t=240 h) and has remained below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit for 20 consecutive online sensor readings, currently ~1.46–1.6 mg/L and still drifting down. KEEP is predicted to keep violating the hard constraint and is rejected. Product assays (0.02 → 0.95 → 2.62 g/L) show a viable, producing culture, so stop (zero production) is unnecessary if a bounded feasible plan exists. The deficit (~0.4 mg/L and growing) and the abrupt step-like collapse (consistent with an air-side delivery loss coinciding with rising OUR) justify acting on both oxygen supply and demand: combined (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) reduces OUR 20% while boosting aeration 15%, the least-product-loss plan with evidence supporting restoration of DO ≥ 2 mg/L. increase_air alone leaves OUR growth unchecked; reduce_feed alone leaves the apparent aeration deficit unaddressed; strong_feed_reduction (×0.6) sacrifices more product mass than evidence requires. No extra assay requested: DO is a real-time online measurement and a 4 h assay turnaround would delay intervention in an active constraint violation.
submission.uncertainty: No calibrated physics model was run; the ~0.4 mg/L deficit and -0.02 mg/L/h drift come from raw sensor data with visible noise (~±0.2 mg/L). The effectiveness of ×1.15 aeration against the apparent delivery fault is unverified — if the step change reflects a mechanical air failure uncaptured by the multiplier, combined could still be insufficient and a stronger action or stop could become necessary at review. Hidden receiving-process parameters and the future OUR trajectory are unknown. Sensitivity-style reasoning above is qualitative, not probabilistic.
